subject: Renewal proposal v3: usage tiers, uplift guardrails, and review cadence
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Sutton <emma@brightbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal proposal v3: usage tiers, uplift guardrails, and review cadence

Hi Emma —

Thanks again for the candid conversation last week. Attached is proposal v3 (redwood-proposal-BrightBank-v3.pdf) that incorporates BrightBank's usage profile and our recommended guardrails to limit surprise uplift at renewal. High level:

- Term: 12 months (renewal at month 12)
- Commit tiers (monthly equivalent):
  • Tier A: up to 100M tokens — $0.0012 / token
  • Tier B: 100M–500M tokens — $0.00095 / token
  • Tier C: >500M tokens — $0.00078 / token
- Uplift protection: first renewal uplift capped at 20% (relative to year-1 blended effective rate).
- True-up windows: quarterly true-up with a 60-day reporting window; midterm 6-month checkpoint with optional repricing if usage deviates >40% from forecast.
- Early termination / overage: overage charged at Tier B rate until next true-up.

I've included the usage export (BrightBank-usage-breakdown-Q1.csv) to show where we expect growth and where caching/batching will have the most impact. The DocuSign link will be ready once we align on the uplift cap and true-up cadence.

As a next step, can you confirm whether procurement needs the uplift cap lowered to 15% to take this to legal, or if 20% is acceptable? If 20% is okay, I'll send the DocuSign.

Best,
Priyom
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
priYom.das@redwood.ai | +1 415 555 0132

Attachments: redwood-proposal-BrightBank-v3.pdf (PDF), BrightBank-usage-breakdown-Q1.csv (CSV)

From: Emma Sutton <emma@brightbank.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@brightbank.com
Date: 2027-05-09T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal v3: usage tiers, uplift guardrails, and review cadence

Thanks, Priyom. Appreciate the quick turn. A few immediate questions/asks from our side:

1) Uplift cap — procurement pushed back: 15% round-1 cap is their preference. They said 20% will make internal approval slower. Can you do 15% for the first renewal?

2) Midterm repricing — BrightBank is sensitive to step changes. If we accept a cap, we also need an explicit commitment to a six-month usage review and a rightsized discount if utilization drops below 70% of forecast.

3) Proof points — legal wants a short note on how Redwood's caching/batching means our effective per-token rate is unlikely to spike dramatically; can you add a 1-paragraph tech note or point me to a short doc?

We want to move quickly, so if you can update the proposal with a 15% cap + 6-month review language and the tech note, procurement will fast-track.

On Sun, May 9, 2027 at 9:12 AM Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks again for the candid conversation last week. Attached is proposal v3...

–Emma Sutton
Head of AI Ops | BrightBank
emma@brightbank.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-10T08:00:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Renewal proposal v3: usage tiers, uplift guardrails, and review cadence

Looping in finance and legal context. Quick take:

- 15% uplift cap is tighter than we'd like; risk to unit economics if actual growth > forecast.
- Mitigations we can offer to get to 15%: a) require a 12-month term (we already have that), b) include a 6-month mandatory usage checkpoint that can trigger operational remediations (cache tuning, request routing to lower-cost variants), and c) add a staged overage floor (first 10% over forecast billed at Tier B, then immediate true-up).
- We should include a 1-paragraph engineering note that explains prefix/KV caching and batching impact on effective tokens; Ops can draft it. That helps procurement/legal.

If procurement insists on 15% we can accept provided BrightBank signs an acceptance of the midterm review and the staged overage floor. Margin impact: estimated ~3–4% reduction in first-year margin vs. 20% cap, but keeps the deal.

Ben — please confirm the margin hit and approve the exception if acceptable.

Marissa
VP Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Sutton <emma@brightbank.com>, procurement@brightbank.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-11T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Updated proposal and tech note — next steps

Emma / procurement team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the clarity on procurement's preference. We can accommodate a 15% first-renewal uplift cap under the following binding guardrails:

1) 12-month firm term.
2) 6-month mandatory usage checkpoint (within 10 business days of month 6 end) with an operational remediation plan if usage >40% or <70% of forecast.
3) Staged overage floor: first 10% above forecast billed at Tier B rate, subsequent overage reconciled at next true-up.
4) DocuSign will include the above language in section 3.2 (renewal uplift and true-up).

Attached is the updated PDF and a short tech note (below) you can pass to legal. If that looks good I will send the DocuSign link for signatures.

Short tech note for legal: Redwood's serving runtime applies request-aware batching and prefix/KV caching which reduces per-token compute by eliminating redundant context work and increasing effective tokens served per kernel execution. For BrightBank's usage profile (high rate of short chat sessions with common prompts), we estimate 12–18% effective cost reduction versus naive per-request execution. Operational tuning (cache keys, prompt canonicalization) is part of the 6-month checkpoint if utilization patterns diverge.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/tx/XYZ-998233
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/8742

Can we have procurement confirm by EOD Wednesday 2027-05-12 so legal can prepare?

Thanks —
Priyom
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
